tagline: A global leader in publishing, travel retail and live entertainment with diversified geographic presence
hero_kpi_rationale: Solid 3.8% comparable growth driven by all business segments (Publishing, Travel Retail and Live Entertainment), reflecting the group's operational and geographic diversification amid an uncertain geopolitical environment.

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.explanation: Total value of sales generated by the consolidated group.
kpis.description: Group revenue increased thanks to strong performance across all activities, particularly Travel Retail and Lagardère Live, despite geopolitical tensions.
kpis.signal: Solid 3.8% growth on a comparable basis

kpis.name: Publishing Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue generated from book, magazine, and board game publishing.
kpis.description: Driven by literary successes in France and the United States, along with board games growing 10% and magazine collections up 8%.
kpis.signal: Growth despite difficult market conditions in the UK, supported by literary hits and board games up 10%

kpis.name: Travel Retail Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue from stores in airports, train stations, and other travel hubs.
kpis.description: Driven by North America, Europe, and recovery in Auckland, despite rationalization in China and the impact of the Middle East conflict in late February 2026.
kpis.signal: Sustained growth driven by North America (+7%), Europe and Asia-Pacific despite tensions

kpis.name: Live Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue from media, radio, shows, and events.
kpis.description: Driven by Lagardère Live Entertainment and continued audience growth at Europe 1 and Europe 2, as well as favorable timing of artist tours.
kpis.signal: Continued growth momentum despite challenging advertising market

kpis.name: Geographic Mix - US & Canada
kpis.explanation: Proportion of revenue generated in North America.
kpis.description: The United States and Canada represent 27% of consolidated revenue, down 1 percentage point from 28% in Q1 2025.
kpis.signal: Slight 1 percentage point decline reflecting geographic diversification

kpis.name: Geographic Mix - France
kpis.explanation: Share of revenue generated in France.
kpis.description: France represents 20% of consolidated revenue, compared to 21% a year earlier, reflecting increased international exposure.

risks.title: Dependence on editorial successes and IP concentration
risks.score_rationale: Major risk for Lagardère Publishing: growth relies on a few key titles (Verity Hoover, Quicksilver Hart, Rebecca Yarros). Central position in Item 1A implied through detailed author-level sales. Intensive language around 'success' and 'momentum' of specific titles. Trend stable but high structural vulnerability.

risks.title: Volatility in airport markets and concession dependency
risks.score_rationale: Lagardère Travel Retail (66% of revenue) is fully dependent on airport concession contracts. Item 1A mentions acquisitions (Amsterdam Schiphol May 2025, Auckland March 2025) and closures (China -28%). Moderate language but high structural risk: renegotiations, non-renewals, airport regulation. Trend up (new concessions) but inherent volatility.

risks.title: Geographic exposure and air traffic volatility
risks.score_rationale: Travel Retail exposes the group to economic cycles and air traffic: Asia-Pacific -24% (North Asia -28%), Americas +2% (North America +1% despite -1% traffic). Item 1A provides regional detail. Neutral language but material impact on 66% of revenue. Trend down in some regions, up in Africa (+16%). High geopolitical and macroeconomic risk.

risks.title: Integration and amortization of acquisitions (Sterling, 999 Games)
risks.score_rationale: Lagardère Publishing acquired Sterling Publishing (Nov 2024) and 999 Games (Apr 2025). Item 1A mentions -3 M€ integration costs for Sterling and -54 M€ amortization of intangibles related to acquisitions. Moderate language but risk of operational integration and unrealized synergies. Trend new (recent acquisitions).

risks.title: Cybersecurity and protection of customer/author data
risks.score_rationale: Lagardère operates in publishing (author data, contracts), retail (customer data, payments), and media (journalistic data). Item 1A does not explicitly mention cybersecurity, but lack of disclosure suggests a risk not publicly managed. Trend stable but increasing sector severity. Absence of language = high implicit risk.

risks.title: Intense competition in publishing and airport retail
risks.score_rationale: Publishing: Hachette Book Group becomes 3rd largest US publisher (source Circana), but faces Amazon, Penguin Random House, Simon & Schuster. Travel Retail: competition from other operators (Paradies, Dufry) for airport contracts. Item 1A implies this through moderate growth (1% comparable Publishing). Neutral language but structural competitive pressure.

risks.title: Risk of impairments on goodwill and intangible assets
risks.score_rationale: Item 1A reports -8 M€ impairments in H1 2025 (including -6 M€ on equity-method investments in Poland). Amortization of intangibles at -61 M€ (including -54 M€ from Travel Retail concessions). Factual language but risk of future deterioration if operational performance weakens. Trend stable but vulnerable to economic shocks.

risks.title: Dependence on key partners and suppliers (distribution, authors)
risks.score_rationale: Publishing: reliance on successful authors and distributors (e.g., Bloomsbury partnership April 2025). Travel Retail: dependence on airports and luxury/travel essentials brands. Item 1A mentions Bloomsbury partnership but limited detail on supplier risks. Neutral language. Trend stable but moderate structural risk.
